decisions.reason: As a newly launched resin injection unit in the firm’s core application-technology business, it is still an option with unresolved market potential and likely modest holding cost relative to the value of learning.

Although it overlaps with another new two-component resin injection unit and so faces some pruning risk, the firm would usually keep it another year to learn which specification customers prefer before abandoning it.

An automatic airless spray gun fits closely with the company’s established spraying portfolio, so a medium-sized German machinery firm would normally leave it on the market while demand uncertainty resolves.
A manual airless spray gun is highly aligned with the firm’s core products and distribution channels, making it inexpensive to keep and premature to drop after only one year.

The air-assisted airless spray gun extends an existing technology family, and real-options logic favors retaining such a related product when evidence is still limited and support capabilities already exist.

The data logger is somewhat more uncertain because it is a more digital, adjunct product, but it supports the firm’s innovation path and is still worth keeping as a low-commitment option for another year.
